# QA Report: Measurement Guide Web Page

## 1. Profile Tabs (For Men / For Women / For Children)
**Status: ✅ PASS**
- All three tabs are present and clearly visible in the center of the page.
- **Switching behavior confirmed**: 
  - Screenshot 1 shows **"For women"** active (dark pill), displaying female-specific measurements (Bust, Underbust, Natural waist, Hips, Shoulder width, Sleeve length, Dress/skirt length).
  - Screenshots 2 & 3 show **"For children"** active, displaying child-specific measurements (Height, Chest, Waist, Hips, Sleeve, Inside leg).
  - The descriptive text below the tabs changes contextually ("Dresses, blouses..." for women vs. "Uniforms and growing bodies..." for children).

## 2. Interactive Line-Art Human Figure Diagram
**Status: ⚠️ CONDITIONAL PASS (See Issues)**

**General Quality**: The diagrams use a clean, minimalist croquis style (thin grey lines) which looks premium and anatomically sensible at first glance.

**Detailed Findings by Screenshot**:

**Screenshot 1 (Women - "Bust" selected):**
- **Figure**: Female silhouette with subtle bust curve indication.
- **Active Line**: Horizontal gold line across the chest labeled "**Bust**" with endpoints marked.
- **Labeling**: Labels for Shoulder, Bust, Underbust, Sleeve, Waist, and Hips are present.
- **Issue**: The "**Underbust**" label on the right side is positioned very close to the body outline; depending on screen resolution, it may appear slightly cramped against the line art. Otherwise, placement is clean.

**Screenshot 2 (Children - "Height" selected):**
- **Figure**: Child proportion figure (shorter torso, slightly larger head ratio relative to body).
- **Active Line**: Vertical gold line running from the top of the head to the floor, labeled "**Height**".
- **Labeling**: Shows Chest, Sleeve, Waist, Hips labels.
- **Critical Layout Issue**: The "**Height**" label and its vertical line extend to the **left** of the figure's feet. While not strictly "floating," it breaks the visual container symmetry. More importantly, the label appears to sit outside the main card padding or very close to the left edge of the diagram area.

**Screenshot 3 (Children - "Waist" selected):**
- **Same child figure**, now showing horizontal gold line for "**Waist**".
- **Labeling**: Height (vertical line now inactive/grey), Waist (active), plus Chest, Hips.
- **Legibility**: Good. No overlapping text detected in this view.

## 3. Gender/Age Appropriate Differentiation
**Status: ✅ PASS**
- **Women vs. Men** (inferred from Screenshot 1): The diagram clearly includes **Bust** and **Underbust** measurement points with appropriate curvature suggestions in the line art, distinct from a male chest measurement.
- **Children vs. Adults** (Screenshots 2 & 3): The child figure is noticeably **shorter with a larger head-to-body ratio** (approximately 1:4 or 1:5 vs adult 1:7.5). The measurement set correctly swaps "Neck/Chest/Shoulder" priorities for "**Height**" and "**Inside leg**" (growth metrics).

## 4. Measurement Detail Cards
**Status: ✅ PASS**
All three screenshots show the detail card structure fully populated:
- **Header**: Measurement name (e.g., "Bust", "Height", "Waist") + Context tag ("Women's measurement" / "Children's measurement").
- **Definition**: Clear one-line description.
- **HOW TO MEASURE**: Numbered steps (1, 2, 3...) with circular icons.
- **WHAT THE SEAMSTRESS USES IT FOR**: Dark navy card explaining garment application (e.g., "Dresses, blouses, kaftans..." or "Trousers, skirts...").
- **THE CLASSIC MISTAKE**: Visible at bottom (partially cut off in screenshots but structure exists).

## 5. Layout Issues, Overlaps & Misalignment
**Status: ⚠️ MINOR ISSUES FOUND**

| Issue | Location | Severity | Description |
|-------|----------|----------|-------------|
| **Vertical Line Overflow** | Screenshot 2 (Child Height) | Medium | The vertical "Height" measurement line extends significantly to the left of the figure's base, potentially touching or exceeding the card's left padding boundary. It looks unbalanced compared to the horizontal lines in other views. |
| **Tight Label Spacing** | Screenshot 1 (Women Underbust) | Low | The "Underbust" text on the right side sits very close to the body outline; on smaller mobile screens, this might touch the grey croquis line. |
| **Bottom Content Clipping** | All Screenshots | Low | The "THE CLASSIC MISTAKE" section is cut off at the bottom edge of every screenshot (shows only the header). This suggests either the screenshot crop is tight or the card has excessive internal scrolling/padding pushing content below the fold. |

## 6. Verdict Per Screenshot

### Screenshot 1 (Women / Bust View)
**🟢 SHIP**
- **Top Issue (Minor)**: "Underbust" label proximity to body line—verify on mobile viewport (320px width) that text doesn't overlap the grey anatomy line.
- **Notes**: Clean execution. The interactive highlighting (gold line) works well. The distinction between Bust/Underbust is clear.

### Screenshot 2 (Children / Height View)
**🟡 FIX REQUIRED**
- **Top Issue**: **Vertical "Height" line positioning.** The line drops down the left side of the figure and extends past the feet without clear termination or proper margin handling. It visually "breaks out" of the diagram's balanced layout. Recommend either:
  1. Capping the line with an arrowhead/endpoint at the floor level aligned with the heels.
  2. Moving the "Height" label to the top (above head) or right side to avoid the awkward left-side drop.
  3. Ensuring the line stays within the diagram's safe padding zone.

### Screenshot 3 (Children / Waist View)
**🟢 SHIP**
- **Top Issue (Minor)**: Same clipping observation as others regarding the "Classic Mistake" section being below the fold—ensure users know to scroll within the card if it's a scrollable container, or adjust card height.
- **Notes**: This view demonstrates the interaction working correctly (switching from Height to Waist updates the active line properly). Proportions look correct for a child measurement guide.

---

### Summary Recommendation
**Ship Screenshot 1 & 3 immediately.**  
**Fix Screenshot 2** before release to resolve the awkward vertical line layout for the "Height" measurement on the children's tab—this is the most visually jarring element across all three views and could confuse users about where to measure (the line should clearly indicate crown-to-floor).
